- If sentiment is consistently low or neutral (0.00–0.25) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent periods.  
- When sentiment shows early positive signals (e.g., 0.20–0.40), model underreacts; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with sentiment momentum.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85–90), model tends to hold too high; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overfits recent trends; use 18-day history as anchor and apply smoothing (e.g., 3-point moving average) to reduce volatility bias.  
- If sentiment history shows no change (all 0.00), model tends to forecast flat; introduce slight upward drift (0.5–1.5%) to account for latent market momentum.
